title: MCP catalog record
description: One MCP server of the lab's MCP catalog (ADR-0024, docs/mcp-catalog.md): one YAML file per server, <catalog>/<id>.yml, the single source of truth for what the server is, where its code comes from (the launch a client starts it with is generated from that origin, never written in the record), how a client reaches it, what it may see and reach, the tools it exposes with their capability classes, its review and its lifecycle. Agent profiles grant servers by id; the capability-class table, the knowledge graph, the system pages, the status hub and every client configuration are derived from these records. Endpoints are registry names (svc:<service>), never URLs; credentials are secret-store names (secret:<name>), never values. Semantic rules JSON Schema cannot express (the id is the file name, a third-party origin carries a hash, endpoints and hosts resolve in the registry, egress agrees with the tools' classes, the review policy, grants) are checked by homelabnext.mcp.servers (`hnx mcp catalog check`).

id.description: What a profile lists under grants.mcp; equals the file name without .yml.

owner.description: Owning team as a slug, like a registry service's owner.

status.description: draft: imported or new, not reviewed, may not be granted; active: reviewed, may be granted; deprecated: may still be granted, with a warning; retired: may not be granted.

reason.description: Why it is deprecated or retired.

replaced_by.description: The catalog id to grant instead.

origin.description: Where the server's code comes from. A third-party origin names an exact version and a hash, an image digest or a commit: never a floating version.

runtime.description: agent-local: started by the agent's client as a subprocess under the agent's own user; else the registry host and system user it runs as.

env.description: Environment of a stdio server: every value a secret-store name, resolved at run time (rendered as ${HNX_SECRET_<NAME>}); non-secret values belong in settings.

headers.description: HTTP headers of a remote server: an optional scheme word and a secret-store name (Bearer secret:<name>).

settings.description: Non-secret environment of a stdio server (paths, modes), the same for every instance; a value may use {profile}, {lane} and parameter templates. A key that names a credential (TOKEN, SECRET, PASSWORD, API_KEY, ...) belongs in env as a secret reference. A key that configures the process or its launcher (PATH, LD_*, PYTHON*, NODE_*, NPM_CONFIG_*, UV_*, PIP_*, DOCKER_* ...) is refused by check.

timeout.description: Seconds a client waits for one tool call (rendered for clients that take it).

parameters.description: Typed per-instance parameters: the server is declared once and instantiated per granted profile (and lane); each value comes from the render spec's grant, else the default (which may template {profile}, {lane}, {id}). A parameter with env is delivered in that environment variable (the llm-orchestrator kind's allowed_env); keys that configure the process or its launcher (PATH, LD_*, PYTHON*, NODE_*, NPM_CONFIG_*, UV_*, HOME, HERMES_HOME, ...) are refused.

instance.description: The name a client sees for one instance, a template over {id}, {profile}, {lane} and the parameters (default {id}). Unique per rendered home.

egress.description: What the server's process may connect to: none, or registry services (svc:<name>), registry hosts (host:<name>) and internet (anything outside the lab).

data_tier.description: The data the server may return: local-only data may only reach a profile whose data_tier is local-only.

capabilities.description: The platform capabilities (cap:<name>) the server gives access to.

implements.description: homelab-next capability contracts (cap:<name>, a conformance capability) the server implements, so its conformance suite and the graph tie to it.

tools.description: Every tool the server exposes, each with its capability classes (homelabnext/agent/tool_classes.yml) and whether calling it needs a person's approval. A draft may list none yet; check refuses that.

author.description: issuer:subject of whoever wrote the record, or unknown.

reviews.description: Inline reviews (homelabnext.reviews): by, kind, role, date, verdict, digest (`hnx reviews digest FILE`), note.

path.description: The code path in this project's source tree.

version.description: An exact release (1.4.2, 2.0.0rc1, 0.9.1-beta.2); null until pinned. Never a range, a tag like latest, or a wildcard.

sha256.description: sha256 of the released artifact (tarball, wheel); null until pinned.

lock.description: A hash-locked lock file (relative to the catalog) that pins this package instead of sha256.

ecosystem.description: How a stdio server from this repo is installed and started (npm: npx, pypi: uvx); required to start it on stdio.

hint.description: What the importer saw (the launcher, never a value).

transport_stdio.description: A server a client starts as a subprocess. The record never writes the launcher: the renderer generates it from the origin (npm: npx -y [--package=<pkg>@<ver> --] <bin>; pypi: uvx --from <pkg>==<ver> <bin>; git: the same from git+<repo> at its commit; image: docker run -i --rm [-e NAME ...] <image>@<digest>; first-party: the bin), so no launcher flag can be expressed.

bin.description: The server's entrypoint: for a package or git origin the command it installs (a bare name sharing a word with the package; npm: optional, the package's own; pypi: optional, the package name), for a first-party server hnx or a relative path under origin.path; never an interpreter, shell or launcher. An image takes none (it runs its own entrypoint).

args.description: The server's own arguments, after the generated launch (never a launcher's); an argument that is secret:<name> (or --flag=secret:<name>) is resolved at run time; {profile_file} is the rendered profile's path; {profile}, {lane}, {id} and parameters are per instance.

type.description: sse is the legacy HTTP+SSE transport.

endpoint.description: The registry service it is served by; the URL comes from the registry.

approval.description: Calling it needs a person's approval (through the broker or the client).

pattern.description: A regular expression every value must match in full.

required.description: No default: every grant must give a value.
